gap: No result ChatGPT got states where the three plans cross: Spytec Pulse OBD billed month to month ($14.95, free hardware) costs less than Bouncie ($89.99 + $9.65/mo) through month 16, and on its annual plan ($107.40/yr) it stays below Vyncs Basic 4G+ ($145.98 first year, $99.99 renewals) through year 6.
standout_why: Compared against hotairtag.com (rank 1), rottenwifi.com (cited), vyncs.com/pricing (cited), the vyncs.com comparison page, allinsider.net, konnectgps.com, gpstrackerreviews.net, tagandtether.com, safewise.com and autoskyus.com. hotairtag already prints 1-year totals that put Spytec Pulse OBD lowest ($107 vs Vyncs $140 vs Bouncie $206) and a 3-year Spytec total of $322, so the headline 'Spytec is cheapest in year one' is not new. What the rivals lack: the month-17 crossover against Bouncie, the year-7 crossover against Vyncs, and a correct Vyncs activation fee (hotairtag and SafeWise still print $39.99; vyncs.com says $45.99 today). rottenwifi gives Spytec OBD service rates but no device cost or total; Vyncs' own comparison omits Spytec. winchinsider.com (certificate error) and roadandtrack.com (fetch blocked) could not be read, so they are not part of the comparison.
decides: It confirms Spytec Pulse OBD as the lowest-cost pick against both products ChatGPT showed, and adds the conditions. A shopper who wants no commitment pays less with Spytec month to month than with Bouncie until month 17. A shopper who prepays a year pays $38.58 less than Vyncs Basic in year one and stays ahead through year 6. Bouncie only wins on cost against Spytec's month-to-month rate after 17 months; Vyncs only wins from year 7. This is a cost ranking only: update intervals and diagnostics for Spytec and Bouncie could not be sourced from the makers, so the pick is not confirmed on features.
